subject: Intermittent token-throttle spikes — sync, customer plan, and roadmap asks
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@fastlens.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastlens.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden increases in request latency — starting 08:50 PT

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing a series of 500ms+ burst latencies on our API calls to Redwood starting ~08:50 PT this morning. P95 crawled from ~120ms to ~780ms for about ~30 minutes and we observed some client-side retries. No code changes on our side.

Attached are a cropped trace and the request IDs we collected. Can your team confirm whether there was any capacity reshuffle or routing change from Redwood around that time? This is impacting a few customer-facing flows; we may throttle traffic if it continues.

Thanks,
Tara
Site Reliability Lead, FastLens

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara@fastlens.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increases in request latency — starting 08:50 PT

Thanks for flagging this, Tara — and thanks for the logs.

Ben/Jonas/Mina — can we triage quickly to confirm root cause? Initial notes: customer shows sharp token-generation tail spikes and several throttling (429) events correlated with token-cache eviction windows. Hypothesis: intermittent token-throttling/eviction during autoscaling transitions or batching changes.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can you pull the routing logs + autoscaler events for the FastLens shard between 08:30–09:30 PT?
- Jonas/Mina: can you check if any kernel scheduling or batching parameter changes were deployed to the gen API around that time (deploy history + hotfixes)?
- Product (Grace): if this is a policy/autoscaler interaction, we may need a short-term customer-facing note and a roadmap ask for a more tolerant backoff/kv-cache sticky policy.

I'll coordinate customer comms and propose a brief pause on the FastLens major traffic if we see another spike.

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara@fastlens.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increases in request latency — starting 08:50 PT

Quick update from infra side: pulled the routing/scale logs. Observations:
- Autoscaler triggered two scale-down/scale-up cycles between 08:38–08:55 for the pool serving FastLens (policy: aggressive burst reclaim).
- During the scale events we saw KV-cache evictions for ~7% of active model sessions which led to re-warm (KV fetch + weight swaps) and increased token latencies.
- No kernel rollout or dev deploys in that window. There was a scheduled tuning experiment for continuous-batching that rolled forward at 02:00 PT but no changes this morning.

Preliminary root cause: autoscaler policy + pool compaction resulting in transient KV cache loss for a subset of sessions -> re-warm overhead -> tail latency spikes.

Immediate mitigations I can run now (need approval):
1) Temporarily relax the aggressive reclaim policy for the affected pool (reduce compaction aggressiveness) — low risk, takes ~3m to propagate.
2) Pin FastLens traffic to a sticky subpool for 30–60 minutes to avoid re-warm cycles (higher cost, immediate).

If we go with (1) I think we can avoid a customer-facing throttle. If customer wants guaranteed behavior, (2) is quicker.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara@fastlens.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increases in request latency — starting 08:50 PT

Thanks — confirming Ben's analysis. Additional notes from runtime team:
- The KV-eviction pattern matches an interaction with the compaction window when sequence-length distribution briefly increased due to a FastLens batch job earlier this morning.
- We can deploy a short-term micro-change to the pool allocation logic to prefer sticky assignment for sessions with sustained high prefix lengths; it's low-risk but requires a 15–20m rollout and rollback plan.

Proposal (recommended):
A) Immediate: Ben relaxes reclaim (option 1) now to stop further evictions.
B) Short-term (next 1–2 hours): we pin FastLens to a sticky subpool for the next 60 minutes to ensure no further re-warms while we monitor.
C) Medium-term roadmap ask: product to prioritize sticky-assignment policy and autoscaler tradeoff tuning in the upcoming sprint (Jira RINF-1932).

I'll prepare the exact change and rollback steps; Ben, can you make the reclaim change and then we'll do the pin together?

--Jonas
Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Runtime
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@fastlens.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden increases in request latency — Customer note and next steps

Tara — thank you for the quick alert and for the logs. We believe the root cause is an interaction between our autoscaler compaction and KV-cache warming which produced a short burst of tail latency.

Immediate actions we took:
- Relaxed compaction aggressiveness for your serving pool (completed 10:32 PT).
- Pinned FastLens traffic to a sticky subpool for the next 60 minutes while we monitor.

Impact: these changes should stop further KV-eviction re-warms; we expect P95 to return to baseline within ~5–10 minutes of changes taking effect. We'll keep you updated and share a short post-incident note with timeline and long-term mitigations.

Short asks for product/roadmap:
- Priority request: make sticky-assignment for long-prefix sessions a configurable policy (Jira: RINF-1932).
- Consider a safety-window for compaction when model session counts briefly spike (policy tweak).

Attached is a draft of the customer-facing message we plan to send after a final verification pass. Feedback welcome; if okay I'll send a formal post-incident email to FastLens by EOD.

Thanks,
Marissa
[attachment: proposed-customer-note-v1.md]

Marissa / team — thanks for the quick response and the temporary mitigations. P95 is back to the normal range and we didn't observe further retries after the sticky-pin began.

We appreciate the clarity on next steps and the Jira reference. FastLens requests: once you have the post-incident note, include the expected timeline for the sticky-assignment policy and any consumer-configurable knobs we can set. We'll review and open a support ticket for any formal cost/commit implications.

Tara
